analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: CoreWeave 5yr CDS widened another 76bps intraday to a record 1194bps, then closed 30bps tighter at 1086bps after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended the company. CoreWeave equity went from -9.54% at the lows to +5.94% at the close.

Huang said CoreWeave's cost of capital is decreasing. The note says this is true for its current debt, but the market is now pricing a higher cost of capital and higher refinancing costs ahead. The author's chart of the day showed AI-linked financing costs are not excessive relative to the rest of the credit stack, but outliers are emerging (CoreWeave, Oracle).

Oracle fell as much as 8.83% intraday and closed +2.02%. Tech saw broad dip buying. The Philly Semi index was down over 4% early and closed -0.88%, its 7th straight loss. The S&P 500 gained 0.33% with 378 names higher and finished within 1% of its record high. The Nasdaq closed +0.08% after an intraday low of -1.44%.

Kevin Warsh spoke at the IMF conference and did not push back on rate expectations, saying he does not 'prejudge meetings', despite this week's hot inflation data. He was upbeat on a 'massive investment surge' and AI productivity gains. October hike pricing fell to around 15% from roughly 30% as he spoke. S&P and Nasdaq futures turned +0.15%, and Stoxx futures are +0.68%.

Fed speakers were hawkish ahead of the blackout before the October 27-28 meeting. SF Fed's Daly changed her view that the Fed should look through supply shocks, citing overlapping and long-lived shocks. Cleveland Fed's Hammack warned businesses may start building in expectations that prices keep rising.

Global bonds rallied on AI growth concerns despite hawkish US data. The US 2yr fell 5.9bps to 4.74% and the 10yr fell 12.7bps to 5.06%. Bund (-5.3bps), OAT (-8.5bps) and BTP (-6.7bps) 10yr yields also fell. AI growth worries outweighed the inflation impulse for yields.

September US PPI rose +1.3% m/m versus +0.6% expected, the largest monthly jump since March 2022. PPI excluding food, energy and trade services rose +0.5% versus +0.3% expected. Together with CPI, this fed concerns that inflation is broadening beyond energy. Deutsche Bank's US economists project a +0.37% m/m increase in PCE.

US labor and activity data were firm. Initial jobless claims were 199k versus 200k expected, with the 4-week average at 198.5k. September retail sales rose +0.8% versus +0.3% expected. Atlanta Fed GDPNow for Q3 stands at +3.6% annualised.

Asia rebounded after a sharp selloff. KOSPI is up 4.28% after falling nearly 8% yesterday to its lowest close since April. The Nikkei is +1.83%, Hang Seng +1.25%, CSI 300 +0.75% and Shanghai Composite +0.95%. Indonesia's Jakarta Composite is down nearly 11%, its steepest one-day fall since January 1998, after MSCI proposed reclassifying the country from emerging-market to standalone-market status.

Europe was more insulated from AI-related stress. The STOXX 600 rose +0.38% to a 3-week high, with the FTSE 100 +1.08%, CAC 40 +0.78% and FTSE MIB -0.72%. UK August GDP was +0.1% m/m versus -0.1% expected, with 3-month growth at +0.7% versus +0.5% expected. The gilt 10yr yield fell only 5.0bps.
Day ahead: US September industrial production and capacity utilization (DB forecast 0.4% versus 0.4% consensus) and the Euro Area final September CPI.

tension_points.bull_case: Nvidia CEO Huang said CoreWeave's strength is improving and its cost of capital is actually decreasing. CoreWeave equity recovered from -9.54% to +5.94% and CDS tightened 30bps after his comments.
tension_points.bear_case: The cost of capital is lower on the debt it has already issued, but the market is pointing to a higher cost of capital now and increased refinancing costs in the future. The 5yr CDS hit a record 1194bps intraday.

tension_points.theme: AI growth versus inflation for yields
tension_points.bull_case: Slower AI growth pushed yields lower across the board, with the US 10yr down 12.7bps and bunds, OATs and BTPs all lower.
tension_points.bear_case: US data stayed hawkish. PPI jumped +1.3% m/m, retail sales rose +0.8%, and inflation is broadening beyond energy. Daly and Hammack warned about persistent supply shocks.

theme_stances.key_argument: AI-linked financing costs are not excessive relative to the rest of the credit stack for now, but outliers such as CoreWeave and Oracle are starting to emerge.
Hot PPI and CPI data, plus hawkish Fed speakers, point to further Fed tightening even though Warsh did not prejudge the October meeting.
theme_stances.evidence: No rush, but more tightening ahead
